messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran into a deploy failure in staging. Pods for `payments-worker` fail to start because they can't decrypt a secret from KMS after a helm upgrade. Looks like grant missing during deploy. anyone seen this with IRSA + helm hooks?

devon: ugh yeah, common race. is helm creating the SA and the helm chart writing the secret in the same release?

maria: chart creates a k8s ServiceAccount (annotated for IRSA) and then the app init container tries to fetch ciphertext from a k8s secret that we back with a decryption step (external-secrets style). terraform does helm_release -> creates k8s resources, but KMS grant is provisioned by our infra repo (TF). suspect ordering: helm runs before aws_kms_grant exists.

alex: can you paste the TF snippet you're using for the grant & role?

maria: sure — trimmed down:

```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "payments_irsa" {
  name = "payments-irsa-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "app_keys" {
  description = "app keys"
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "payments_decrypt" {
  name = "payments-decrypt-${var.env}"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.app_keys.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.payments_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "DescribeKey"]
}

resource "helm_release" "payments" {
  name       = "payments"
  chart      = "company/payments"
  namespace  = "payments"
  values = [file("./values-${var.env}.yaml")]
}
```

maria: helm_release is in app repo TF; aws_kms_grant is in infra TF -> they run separately during CI pipelines.

devon: yep that matches the race. The grant's principal is the role ARN (good). But if helm runs first, the SA gets annotated, pod assumes role, tries decrypt, fails because grant not present. Options: pre-create grant before helm (preferred), or make helm wait.

samir: for IRSA flow remember the pod actually gets creds via STS assume-role-with-web-identity, so KMS needs to let the role (role arn) call Decrypt. Grant principal = role ARN is fine. Also consider encryption context requirements if you're using them — omitted grants or wrong context will still fail.

alex: practical approaches we use: (1) move aws_kms_grant into infra pipeline that runs before app helm deploy; (2) create the serviceaccount resource in infra (k8s provider) so it's created ahead of helm, then chart uses existing SA; (3) add a TF dependency from helm_release to aws_kms_grant (if they live in same repo) or add a short wait loop in the app CI for grant existence via AWS CLI.

maria: option (1) seems clean: infra pipeline already provisions keys; just ensure grants for roles exist beforehand. worried about number of grants when we have multiple envs/services.

devon: grants are cheap; you can also use a key policy that allows the account (or a limited service principal) to decrypt and avoid many grants, but that widens blast radius. For least privilege, grants per-role are best.

samir: other gotcha: when using Terraform with aws_kms_grant, if the role is replaced (new name/arn), KMS grants don't always update atomically and you can orphan grants. We add lifecycle { prevent_destroy = false }? not ideal. Instead we try to ensure role name stable and reference role by arn.

alex: if you can't change pipeline ordering quickly, a small workaround is to add a pre-install helm hook that sleeps until grant exists. e.g., init hook job that runs `aws kms list-grants --key-id $KEY | jq -r '.. | .GranteePrincipal? | select(.)' | grep $ROLE_ARN` and exits 0 when found.

maria: that could work. i prefer infra-first though. quick question: in the grant code above I used grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.payments_irsa.arn — but our actual role is created by Terraform in a different state (app state). any way to reference it without cross-state import?

devon: either export the role ARN as an output from app TF and fetch it in infra via remote state data source, or create the role in infra. remote state read is simplest: data.terraform_remote_state.app.outputs.payments_irsa_arn. Make sure ordering: infra pipeline reads remote state that already contains role. But that reintroduces ordering requirements.

samir: alternative: use an assume-role principal that matches the OIDC provider + role session name? not workable for KMS grant; KMS grant wants a principal ARN (IAM role/user).

alex: FYI we had an intermittent on prod where helm hooks created sealed secret before grant; fix was: in infra pipeline add a step to create grants for all known service roles for env before app deploys. simple and reliable.

maria: ok i'll try: 1) open infra PR to add grants for payments service role and run infra pipeline earlier in pipeline; 2) short-term add helm init hook that waits for grant so we don't block staging deploys.

devon: sgtm. when you open PR ping me for review — i'll double-check grant lifecycle bits.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please ensure aws_kms_grant resources have `depends_on = [aws_kms_key.app_keys]` and the grant name is stable to aid audits.

maria: noted. one more tiny Q — any reason to prefer key policy over grants for this?

samir: key policy can be simpler: you can allow the entire account's roles to use key if you narrow on conditions (aws:PrincipalArn like arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/company-*). But KMS key policy condition language for ARN matching is funky. Grants are explicit and easy to audit per role. choose based on how many roles you need and your security posture.

maria: thanks all — will push infra PR + chart change. i'll paste links when ready. :thumbsup:
